name: Operation Broken Chains
summary: Hypothetical scenario: the resistance and the coalition help the people of an invented provincial city take back their streets. Free the detained, retake the radio station and offer the security garrison a way to surrender.

states.objective: Briefing: Shahrbaran is rising. Help the people take the city without turning it into a battlefield.
Fly Raven over the bridges, the bazaar and the hospital district. Mark where civilians are sheltering.
Choose the opening move. Hold the bridges so aid and guards can enter, or secure the bazaar first and shelter the crowds.
Take the river bridges so the guard force and the aid convoy can cross.
Move through the bazaar quarter and bring the crowds to safe ground.
Secure the old bazaar quarter and shelter the crowds before the regime cordon closes.
Take the river bridges so the aid convoy can cross.
Free the people held in the security detention compound. Guards who lay down their weapons are protected too.
Retake the city radio station so the people hear the truth and the garrison hears the surrender offer.
Deliver aid to the hospital district.
Offer the security headquarters garrison the chance to surrender. Hardliners may refuse; conscripts often will not.
Debrief: the state of the city, the civilians sheltered and the soldiers who surrendered.
Shahrbaran is free. The detained are home, the hospital works and the garrison has surrendered.
Shahrbaran is free, but the city was damaged or civilians paid a price. Its people are wary.
The operation failed: the uprising was crushed or too many civilians were harmed. Restart from the last checkpoint.
